chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Hariz from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Pray to your Lord and slaughter.' He said, 'Slaughtering is balance in standing, that he straightens his back and neck.' And he said, 'Do not fold your arms; only the Magians do that. And do not cover your mouth, and do not be hasty, and do not sit on your heels, and do not spread your forearms.'

key_terms.النَّحْرُ: Slaughtering; here used metaphorically for straightening the neck and back in prayer
key_terms.الِاعْتِدَالُ: Balance/Equilibrium; the state of proper posture
key_terms.الْقِيَامُ: Standing; the first pillar of prayer
key_terms.اِفْتِرَاشٌ: Spreading the forearms on the ground
key_terms.تَكْفِيرٌ: Folding arms; specifically referring to the practice of the Magians

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended and prohibited postures for the standing position in Shia prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the physical posture of *qiyam* by interpreting the phrase 'sacrifice for your Lord' as maintaining bodily straightness, while distinguishing Islamic prayer etiquette from Zoroastrian practices by prohibiting arm-folding. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *i'tidal* (uprightness) in worship, rejecting both excessive haste and rigid imitation of other faiths. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the prophetic tradition of prayer as a balanced act of devotion that mirrors inner composure.
